- [guideline] **Streaming-render cost lives in the renderer, not the transport — gate the expensive parse on `isStreaming`** (run_00e0e872, 2026-06-26) — "Streaming feels janky on long replies" was NOT a transport/SSE/store problem (those were all confirmed per-token-immediate + rAF-coalesced). The cost was `ContentBlockRenderer:50` feeding a growing `block.text` into MarkdownRenderer (4 remark/rehype plugins + KaTeX + highlight.js) on EVERY token → O(n²) re-parse over the stream. Fix = render plaintext (`whitespace-pre-wrap`) while `isStreaming`, switch to markdown on finish (the unchanged path every historical message already uses). Three reusable points: (1) when a "feels slow" complaint hits a streaming UI, profile the RENDER leaf before the data layer — per-token full re-parse is the classic O(n²) trap; (2) the safest perf fix on a bug-sensitive frontend is a presentation-leaf conditional that reads state and writes none — blast radius is provably zero (adversarial verified a-e); (3) the cross-tab stuck-state fear (OT01/COE07-09 history) was structurally absent BECAUSE `isStreaming` is per-tab + only the re-render-triggering `setIsStreaming` writes it + a 30s reconcile loop force-clears — proving the single-writer + reconcile-backstop architecture pays off when adding new state-dependent render branches.
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **After N transport-layer fixes don't hold, the bug is in the layer you never touched** (reconcile-gap, run_9db9f987, 2026-06-25) — The #1 recurring bug (COE07/08/09, ~33 patches over months) was a *truncated render after tab-switch*. Every prior fix targeted backend persistence / SSE / store-reconcile / boundary-dedup — and the bug always recurred because those layers were already innocent (store-level reconcile always returned full text). The actual defect was the React **render-source selector** (`TabView.tsx:152` dual-source `store ?? stale-prop` fallback) — a layer no prior fix had inspected. Fix = enforce ONE render source (MessageStore only; prop-fallback deleted), making divergence structurally impossible. Two meta-lessons: (1) when repeated fixes at one layer don't converge, STOP patching that layer and audit the untouched neighbor; (2) the entry was a LIVE DEV-gated repro probe, not another static patch — the bug was unreproducible at every statically-testable layer, so only live observation localized it (this was the long-standing P0 in Open Threads OT01).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **Unify scattered deciders by DELEGATION, not ABSORPTION, when the old unit is heavily tested** (RecoveryCoordinator, run_4988bfb4, 2026-06-25) — 8 independent kill-deciders unified into one RecoveryCoordinator. The blast-radius check decided the shape: HealingLoop had 1 prod caller but **5 test files** → the coordinator HOLDS HealingLoop (delegates breaker state) instead of replacing it, so all 5 test files stayed green untouched (DEC06). Owns only the DECISION (may-recover + what-kind + escalation); kill MECHANICS stay in SessionUnit. Multi-shape unification rule (PIT17): share what is TRULY universal (the enabled/user_stopped guard + the 7-verdict vocabulary), DISPATCH what differs (the gate — attempt-breaker vs cooldown vs bare-threshold vs graceful-escalation). The RecoveryTransaction lock then closed the `_crash_to_cold` TOCTOU (N concurrent callers → exactly 1 teardown) — recovery paths MUST have a forced-execution test (STEERING #11; the `self._pid` AttributeError class proved "compiles ≠ executes").
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **PermissionError is not ProcessLookupError** -- `os.kill(pid, 0)` raises `PermissionError` (subclass of `OSError`) for processes owned by other users. Catching `(OSError, ProcessLookupError)` treats alive-but-unowned processes as dead. Fix: catch `PermissionError` separately and treat as "alive". This matters for daemon conflict checks where the daemon runs as the same user but PID 1 (launchd) owns the port check socket. Pattern: any PID liveness check must handle 3 states: alive+ours, alive+theirs (PermissionError), dead (ProcessLookupError).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived -->

- [guideline] **Streaming-render cost lives in the renderer, not the transport — gate the expensive parse on `isStreaming`** (run_00e0e872, 2026-06-26) — "Streaming feels janky on long replies" was NOT a transport/SSE/store problem (those were all confirmed per-token-immediate + rAF-coalesced). The cost was `ContentBlockRenderer:50` feeding a growing `block.text` into MarkdownRenderer (4 remark/rehype plugins + KaTeX + highlight.js) on EVERY token → O(n²) re-parse over the stream. Fix = render plaintext (`whitespace-pre-wrap`) while `isStreaming`, switch to markdown on finish (the unchanged path every historical message already uses). Three reusable points: (1) when a "feels slow" complaint hits a streaming UI, profile the RENDER leaf before the data layer — per-token full re-parse is the classic O(n²) trap; (2) the safest perf fix on a bug-sensitive frontend is a presentation-leaf conditional that reads state and writes none — blast radius is provably zero (adversarial verified a-e); (3) the cross-tab stuck-state fear (OT01/COE07-09 history) was structurally absent BECAUSE `isStreaming` is per-tab + only the re-render-triggering `setIsStreaming` writes it + a 30s reconcile loop force-clears — proving the single-writer + reconcile-backstop architecture pays off when adding new state-dependent render branches.
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **After N transport-layer fixes don't hold, the bug is in the layer you never touched** (reconcile-gap, run_9db9f987, 2026-06-25) — The #1 recurring bug (COE07/08/09, ~33 patches over months) was a *truncated render after tab-switch*. Every prior fix targeted backend persistence / SSE / store-reconcile / boundary-dedup — and the bug always recurred because those layers were already innocent (store-level reconcile always returned full text). The actual defect was the React **render-source selector** (`TabView.tsx:152` dual-source `store ?? stale-prop` fallback) — a layer no prior fix had inspected. Fix = enforce ONE render source (MessageStore only; prop-fallback deleted), making divergence structurally impossible. Two meta-lessons: (1) when repeated fixes at one layer don't converge, STOP patching that layer and audit the untouched neighbor; (2) the entry was a LIVE DEV-gated repro probe, not another static patch — the bug was unreproducible at every statically-testable layer, so only live observation localized it (this was the long-standing P0 in Open Threads OT01).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **Unify scattered deciders by DELEGATION, not ABSORPTION, when the old unit is heavily tested** (RecoveryCoordinator, run_4988bfb4, 2026-06-25) — 8 independent kill-deciders unified into one RecoveryCoordinator. The blast-radius check decided the shape: HealingLoop had 1 prod caller but **5 test files** → the coordinator HOLDS HealingLoop (delegates breaker state) instead of replacing it, so all 5 test files stayed green untouched (DEC06). Owns only the DECISION (may-recover + what-kind + escalation); kill MECHANICS stay in SessionUnit. Multi-shape unification rule (PIT17): share what is TRULY universal (the enabled/user_stopped guard + the 7-verdict vocabulary), DISPATCH what differs (the gate — attempt-breaker vs cooldown vs bare-threshold vs graceful-escalation). The RecoveryTransaction lock then closed the `_crash_to_cold` TOCTOU (N concurrent callers → exactly 1 teardown) — recovery paths MUST have a forced-execution test (STEERING #11; the `self._pid` AttributeError class proved "compiles ≠ executes").
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **PermissionError is not ProcessLookupError** -- `os.kill(pid, 0)` raises `PermissionError` (subclass of `OSError`) for processes owned by other users. Catching `(OSError, ProcessLookupError)` treats alive-but-unowned processes as dead. Fix: catch `PermissionError` separately and treat as "alive". This matters for daemon conflict checks where the daemon runs as the same user but PID 1 (launchd) owns the port check socket. Pattern: any PID liveness check must handle 3 states: alive+ours, alive+theirs (PermissionError), dead (ProcessLookupError).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived -->

- [guideline] **Streaming-render cost lives in the renderer, not the transport — gate the expensive parse on `isStreaming`** (run_00e0e872, 2026-06-26) — "Streaming feels janky on long replies" was NOT a transport/SSE/store problem (those were all confirmed per-token-immediate + rAF-coalesced). The cost was `ContentBlockRenderer:50` feeding a growing `block.text` into MarkdownRenderer (4 remark/rehype plugins + KaTeX + highlight.js) on EVERY token → O(n²) re-parse over the stream. Fix = render plaintext (`whitespace-pre-wrap`) while `isStreaming`, switch to markdown on finish (the unchanged path every historical message already uses). Three reusable points: (1) when a "feels slow" complaint hits a streaming UI, profile the RENDER leaf before the data layer — per-token full re-parse is the classic O(n²) trap; (2) the safest perf fix on a bug-sensitive frontend is a presentation-leaf conditional that reads state and writes none — blast radius is provably zero (adversarial verified a-e); (3) the cross-tab stuck-state fear (OT01/COE07-09 history) was structurally absent BECAUSE `isStreaming` is per-tab + only the re-render-triggering `setIsStreaming` writes it + a 30s reconcile loop force-clears — proving the single-writer + reconcile-backstop architecture pays off when adding new state-dependent render branches.
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **After N transport-layer fixes don't hold, the bug is in the layer you never touched** (reconcile-gap, run_9db9f987, 2026-06-25) — The #1 recurring bug (COE07/08/09, ~33 patches over months) was a *truncated render after tab-switch*. Every prior fix targeted backend persistence / SSE / store-reconcile / boundary-dedup — and the bug always recurred because those layers were already innocent (store-level reconcile always returned full text). The actual defect was the React **render-source selector** (`TabView.tsx:152` dual-source `store ?? stale-prop` fallback) — a layer no prior fix had inspected. Fix = enforce ONE render source (MessageStore only; prop-fallback deleted), making divergence structurally impossible. Two meta-lessons: (1) when repeated fixes at one layer don't converge, STOP patching that layer and audit the untouched neighbor; (2) the entry was a LIVE DEV-gated repro probe, not another static patch — the bug was unreproducible at every statically-testable layer, so only live observation localized it (this was the long-standing P0 in Open Threads OT01).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **Unify scattered deciders by DELEGATION, not ABSORPTION, when the old unit is heavily tested** (RecoveryCoordinator, run_4988bfb4, 2026-06-25) — 8 independent kill-deciders unified into one RecoveryCoordinator. The blast-radius check decided the shape: HealingLoop had 1 prod caller but **5 test files** → the coordinator HOLDS HealingLoop (delegates breaker state) instead of replacing it, so all 5 test files stayed green untouched (DEC06). Owns only the DECISION (may-recover + what-kind + escalation); kill MECHANICS stay in SessionUnit. Multi-shape unification rule (PIT17): share what is TRULY universal (the enabled/user_stopped guard + the 7-verdict vocabulary), DISPATCH what differs (the gate — attempt-breaker vs cooldown vs bare-threshold vs graceful-escalation). The RecoveryTransaction lock then closed the `_crash_to_cold` TOCTOU (N concurrent callers → exactly 1 teardown) — recovery paths MUST have a forced-execution test (STEERING #11; the `self._pid` AttributeError class proved "compiles ≠ executes").
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **PermissionError is not ProcessLookupError** -- `os.kill(pid, 0)` raises `PermissionError` (subclass of `OSError`) for processes owned by other users. Catching `(OSError, ProcessLookupError)` treats alive-but-unowned processes as dead. Fix: catch `PermissionError` separately and treat as "alive". This matters for daemon conflict checks where the daemon runs as the same user but PID 1 (launchd) owns the port check socket. Pattern: any PID liveness check must handle 3 states: alive+ours, alive+theirs (PermissionError), dead (ProcessLookupError).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived -->

- [guideline] **Streaming-render cost lives in the renderer, not the transport — gate the expensive parse on `isStreaming`** (run_00e0e872, 2026-06-26) — "Streaming feels janky on long replies" was NOT a transport/SSE/store problem (those were all confirmed per-token-immediate + rAF-coalesced). The cost was `ContentBlockRenderer:50` feeding a growing `block.text` into MarkdownRenderer (4 remark/rehype plugins + KaTeX + highlight.js) on EVERY token → O(n²) re-parse over the stream. Fix = render plaintext (`whitespace-pre-wrap`) while `isStreaming`, switch to markdown on finish (the unchanged path every historical message already uses). Three reusable points: (1) when a "feels slow" complaint hits a streaming UI, profile the RENDER leaf before the data layer — per-token full re-parse is the classic O(n²) trap; (2) the safest perf fix on a bug-sensitive frontend is a presentation-leaf conditional that reads state and writes none — blast radius is provably zero (adversarial verified a-e); (3) the cross-tab stuck-state fear (OT01/COE07-09 history) was structurally absent BECAUSE `isStreaming` is per-tab + only the re-render-triggering `setIsStreaming` writes it + a 30s reconcile loop force-clears — proving the single-writer + reconcile-backstop architecture pays off when adding new state-dependent render branches.
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **After N transport-layer fixes don't hold, the bug is in the layer you never touched** (reconcile-gap, run_9db9f987, 2026-06-25) — The #1 recurring bug (COE07/08/09, ~33 patches over months) was a *truncated render after tab-switch*. Every prior fix targeted backend persistence / SSE / store-reconcile / boundary-dedup — and the bug always recurred because those layers were already innocent (store-level reconcile always returned full text). The actual defect was the React **render-source selector** (`TabView.tsx:152` dual-source `store ?? stale-prop` fallback) — a layer no prior fix had inspected. Fix = enforce ONE render source (MessageStore only; prop-fallback deleted), making divergence structurally impossible. Two meta-lessons: (1) when repeated fixes at one layer don't converge, STOP patching that layer and audit the untouched neighbor; (2) the entry was a LIVE DEV-gated repro probe, not another static patch — the bug was unreproducible at every statically-testable layer, so only live observation localized it (this was the long-standing P0 in Open Threads OT01).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **Unify scattered deciders by DELEGATION, not ABSORPTION, when the old unit is heavily tested** (RecoveryCoordinator, run_4988bfb4, 2026-06-25) — 8 independent kill-deciders unified into one RecoveryCoordinator. The blast-radius check decided the shape: HealingLoop had 1 prod caller but **5 test files** → the coordinator HOLDS HealingLoop (delegates breaker state) instead of replacing it, so all 5 test files stayed green untouched (DEC06). Owns only the DECISION (may-recover + what-kind + escalation); kill MECHANICS stay in SessionUnit. Multi-shape unification rule (PIT17): share what is TRULY universal (the enabled/user_stopped guard + the 7-verdict vocabulary), DISPATCH what differs (the gate — attempt-breaker vs cooldown vs bare-threshold vs graceful-escalation). The RecoveryTransaction lock then closed the `_crash_to_cold` TOCTOU (N concurrent callers → exactly 1 teardown) — recovery paths MUST have a forced-execution test (STEERING #11; the `self._pid` AttributeError class proved "compiles ≠ executes").
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **PermissionError is not ProcessLookupError** -- `os.kill(pid, 0)` raises `PermissionError` (subclass of `OSError`) for processes owned by other users. Catching `(OSError, ProcessLookupError)` treats alive-but-unowned processes as dead. Fix: catch `PermissionError` separately and treat as "alive". This matters for daemon conflict checks where the daemon runs as the same user but PID 1 (launchd) owns the port check socket. Pattern: any PID liveness check must handle 3 states: alive+ours, alive+theirs (PermissionError), dead (ProcessLookupError).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived -->

The cost was `ContentBlockRenderer:50` feeding a growing `block.text` into MarkdownRenderer (4 remark/rehype plugins + KaTeX + highlight.js) on EVERY token → O(n²) re-parse over the stream. Fix = render plaintext (`whitespace-pre-wrap`) while `isStreaming`, switch to markdown on finish (the unchanged path every historical message already uses). Three reusable points: (1) when a "feels slow" complaint hits a streaming UI, profile the RENDER leaf before the data layer — per-token full re-parse is the classic O(n²) trap; (2) the safest perf fix on a bug-sensitive frontend is a presentation-leaf conditional that reads state and writes none — blast radius is provably zero (adversarial verified a-e); (3) the cross-tab stuck-state fear (OT01/COE07-09 history) was structurally absent BECAUSE `isStreaming` is per-tab + only the re-render-triggering `setIsStreaming` writes it + a 30s reconcile loop force-clears — proving the single-writer + reconcile-backstop architecture pays off when adding new state-dependent render branches.
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **After N transport-layer fixes don't hold, the bug is in the layer you never touched** (reconcile-gap, run_9db9f987, 2026-06-25) — The #1 recurring bug (COE07/08/09, ~33 patches over months) was a *truncated render after tab-switch*. Every prior fix targeted backend persistence / SSE / store-reconcile / boundary-dedup — and the bug always recurred because those layers were already innocent (store-level reconcile always returned full text). The actual defect was the React **render-source selector** (`TabView.tsx:152` dual-source `store ?? stale-prop` fallback) — a layer no prior fix had inspected. Fix = enforce ONE render source (MessageStore only; prop-fallback deleted), making divergence structurally impossible. Two meta-lessons: (1) when repeated fixes at one layer don't converge, STOP patching that layer and audit the untouched neighbor; (2) the entry was a LIVE DEV-gated repro probe, not another static patch — the bug was unreproducible at every statically-testable layer, so only live observation localized it (this was the long-standing P0 in Open Threads OT01).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **Unify scattered deciders by DELEGATION, not ABSORPTION, when the old unit is heavily tested** (RecoveryCoordinator, run_4988bfb4, 2026-06-25) — 8 independent kill-deciders unified into one RecoveryCoordinator. The blast-radius check decided the shape: HealingLoop had 1 prod caller but **5 test files** → the coordinator HOLDS HealingLoop (delegates breaker state) instead of replacing it, so all 5 test files stayed green untouched (DEC06). Owns only the DECISION (may-recover + what-kind + escalation); kill MECHANICS stay in SessionUnit. Multi-shape unification rule (PIT17): share what is TRULY universal (the enabled/user_stopped guard + the 7-verdict vocabulary), DISPATCH what differs (the gate — attempt-breaker vs cooldown vs bare-threshold vs graceful-escalation). The RecoveryTransaction lock then closed the `_crash_to_cold` TOCTOU (N concurrent callers → exactly 1 teardown) — recovery paths MUST have a forced-execution test (STEERING #11; the `self._pid` AttributeError class proved "compiles ≠ executes").

- [decision] **DDD/Library recall boundaries — the CORRECT by-design shape (XG-confirmed 2026-08-15).** Reviewed the whole DDD ingestion+recall chain against the Memory/Evolution 活/冷 experience. Three boundaries are **BY DESIGN, not bugs — do NOT "fix" them:** (1) **Public `Knowledge/Library/` is unconditionally recallable** — it goes through the knowledge_store FTS5 index (`_recall_library`, recall_multi.py:1155; `sync_knowledge_index` scans ALL of `Knowledge/`, `_SKIP_DIRS`={__pycache__,.git,.artifacts} only). Session/project-independent, any query hits it. This MUST stay recallable (it's the cross-project store). (2) **Operational-type DDD entries + other-projects' DDD → FTS5/BM25 on-demand recall is CORRECT** — they are "资料 you look up when relevant", not always-in-context. Query-gated is the right shape for them. (3) **DDD archive (`2-understanding/*-archive*.md`) is NOT recallable, and that is CORRECT** — a DDD entry only reaches archive via age-decay of `guideline`/`process` types (the 5 judgment types decision/model/principle/correction/pitfall are decay-IMMUNE, `EVERGREEN_TYPES`, ddd_entry_lifecycle.py:908; there is NO size-valve on DDD, so nothing high-value is force-archived). Archived DDD = decayed low-value operational info → excluding it from recall is intended (`sync_knowledge_index` deliberately does not scan `2-understanding/`). ⚠️ SUPERSEDES my earlier (2026-08-15, same session) "Gap 1: DDD archive orphan is a bug" framing — XG corrected it: decayed=low-value, archive-not-recalled is by design. - [guideline] **PermissionError is not ProcessLookupError** -- `os.kill(pid, 0)` raises `PermissionError` (subclass of `OSError`) for processes owned by other users. Catching `(OSError, ProcessLookupError)` treats alive-but-unowned processes as dead. Fix: catch `PermissionError` separately and treat as "alive". This matters for daemon conflict checks where the daemon runs as the same user but PID 1 (launchd) owns the port check socket. Pattern: any PID liveness check must handle 3 states: alive+ours, alive+theirs (PermissionError), dead (ProcessLookupError).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived -->

The cost was `ContentBlockRenderer:50` feeding a growing `block.text` into MarkdownRenderer (4 remark/rehype plugins + KaTeX + highlight.js) on EVERY token → O(n²) re-parse over the stream. Fix = render plaintext (`whitespace-pre-wrap`) while `isStreaming`, switch to markdown on finish (the unchanged path every historical message already uses). Three reusable points: (1) when a "feels slow" complaint hits a streaming UI, profile the RENDER leaf before the data layer — per-token full re-parse is the classic O(n²) trap; (2) the safest perf fix on a bug-sensitive frontend is a presentation-leaf conditional that reads state and writes none — blast radius is provably zero (adversarial verified a-e); (3) the cross-tab stuck-state fear (OT01/COE07-09 history) was structurally absent BECAUSE `isStreaming` is per-tab + only the re-render-triggering `setIsStreaming` writes it + a 30s reconcile loop force-clears — proving the single-writer + reconcile-backstop architecture pays off when adding new state-dependent render branches.
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **After N transport-layer fixes don't hold, the bug is in the layer you never touched** (reconcile-gap, run_9db9f987, 2026-06-25) — The #1 recurring bug (COE07/08/09, ~33 patches over months) was a *truncated render after tab-switch*. Every prior fix targeted backend persistence / SSE / store-reconcile / boundary-dedup — and the bug always recurred because those layers were already innocent (store-level reconcile always returned full text). The actual defect was the React **render-source selector** (`TabView.tsx:152` dual-source `store ?? stale-prop` fallback) — a layer no prior fix had inspected. Fix = enforce ONE render source (MessageStore only; prop-fallback deleted), making divergence structurally impossible. Two meta-lessons: (1) when repeated fixes at one layer don't converge, STOP patching that layer and audit the untouched neighbor; (2) the entry was a LIVE DEV-gated repro probe, not another static patch — the bug was unreproducible at every statically-testable layer, so only live observation localized it (this was the long-standing P0 in Open Threads OT01).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **Unify scattered deciders by DELEGATION, not ABSORPTION, when the old unit is heavily tested** (RecoveryCoordinator, run_4988bfb4, 2026-06-25) — 8 independent kill-deciders unified into one RecoveryCoordinator. The blast-radius check decided the shape: HealingLoop had 1 prod caller but **5 test files** → the coordinator HOLDS HealingLoop (delegates breaker state) instead of replacing it, so all 5 test files stayed green untouched (DEC06). Owns only the DECISION (may-recover + what-kind + escalation); kill MECHANICS stay in SessionUnit. Multi-shape unification rule (PIT17): share what is TRULY universal (the enabled/user_stopped guard + the 7-verdict vocabulary), DISPATCH what differs (the gate — attempt-breaker vs cooldown vs bare-threshold vs graceful-escalation). The RecoveryTransaction lock then closed the `_crash_to_cold` TOCTOU (N concurrent callers → exactly 1 teardown) — recovery paths MUST have a forced-execution test (STEERING #11; the `self._pid` AttributeError class proved "compiles ≠ executes").

- [guideline] **PermissionError is not ProcessLookupError** -- `os.kill(pid, 0)` raises `PermissionError` (subclass of `OSError`) for processes owned by other users. Catching `(OSError, ProcessLookupError)` treats alive-but-unowned processes as dead. Fix: catch `PermissionError` separately and treat as "alive". This matters for daemon conflict checks where the daemon runs as the same user but PID 1 (launchd) owns the port check socket. Pattern: any PID liveness check must handle 3 states: alive+ours, alive+theirs (PermissionError), dead (ProcessLookupError).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived -->

Two meta-lessons: (1) when repeated fixes at one layer don't converge, STOP patching that layer and audit the untouched neighbor; (2) the entry was a LIVE DEV-gated repro probe, not another static patch — the bug was unreproducible at every statically-testable layer, so only live observation localized it (this was the long-standing P0 in Open Threads OT01).

- [guideline] **PermissionError is not ProcessLookupError** -- `os.kill(pid, 0)` raises `PermissionError` (subclass of `OSError`) for processes owned by other users. Catching `(OSError, ProcessLookupError)` treats alive-but-unowned processes as dead. Fix: catch `PermissionError` separately and treat as "alive". This matters for daemon conflict checks where the daemon runs as the same user but PID 1 (launchd) owns the port check socket. Pattern: any PID liveness check must handle 3 states: alive+ours, alive+theirs (PermissionError), dead (ProcessLookupError).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived -->

- [guideline] **Streaming-render cost lives in the renderer, not the transport — gate the expensive parse on `isStreaming`** (run_00e0e872, 2026-06-26) — "Streaming feels janky on long replies" was NOT a transport/SSE/store problem (those were all confirmed per-token-immediate + rAF-coalesced). The cost was `ContentBlockRenderer:50` feeding a growing `block.text` into MarkdownRenderer (4 remark/rehype plugins + KaTeX + highlight.js) on EVERY token → O(n²) re-parse over the stream. Fix = render plaintext (`whitespace-pre-wrap`) while `isStreaming`, switch to markdown on finish (the unchanged path every historical message already uses). Three reusable points: (1) when a "feels slow" complaint hits a streaming UI, profile the RENDER leaf before the data layer — per-token full re-parse is the classic O(n²) trap; (2) the safest perf fix on a bug-sensitive frontend is a presentation-leaf conditional that reads state and writes none — blast radius is provably zero (adversarial verified a-e); (3) the cross-tab stuck-state fear (OT01/COE07-09 history) was structurally absent BECAUSE `isStreaming` is per-tab + only the re-render-triggering `setIsStreaming` writes it + a 30s reconcile loop force-clears — proving the single-writer + reconcile-backstop architecture pays off when adding new state-dependent render branches.
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **PermissionError is not ProcessLookupError** -- `os.kill(pid, 0)` raises `PermissionError` (subclass of `OSError`) for processes owned by other users. Catching `(OSError, ProcessLookupError)` treats alive-but-unowned processes as dead. Fix: catch `PermissionError` separately and treat as "alive". This matters for daemon conflict checks where the daemon runs as the same user but PID 1 (launchd) owns the port check socket. Pattern: any PID liveness check must handle 3 states: alive+ours, alive+theirs (PermissionError), dead (ProcessLookupError).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived -->

- [guideline] **Streaming-render cost lives in the renderer, not the transport — gate the expensive parse on `isStreaming`** (run_00e0e872, 2026-06-26) — "Streaming feels janky on long replies" was NOT a transport/SSE/store problem (those were all confirmed per-token-immediate + rAF-coalesced). The cost was `ContentBlockRenderer:50` feeding a growing `block.text` into MarkdownRenderer (4 remark/rehype plugins + KaTeX + highlight.js) on EVERY token → O(n²) re-parse over the stream. Fix = render plaintext (`whitespace-pre-wrap`) while `isStreaming`, switch to markdown on finish (the unchanged path every historical message already uses). Three reusable points: (1) when a "feels slow" complaint hits a streaming UI, profile the RENDER leaf before the data layer — per-token full re-parse is the classic O(n²) trap; (2) the safest perf fix on a bug-sensitive frontend is a presentation-leaf conditional that reads state and writes none — blast radius is provably zero (adversarial verified a-e); (3) the cross-tab stuck-state fear (OT01/COE07-09 history) was structurally absent BECAUSE `isStreaming` is per-tab + only the re-render-triggering `setIsStreaming` writes it + a 30s reconcile loop force-clears — proving the single-writer + reconcile-backstop architecture pays off when adding new state-dependent render branches.
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **After N transport-layer fixes don't hold, the bug is in the layer you never touched** (reconcile-gap, run_9db9f987, 2026-06-25) — The #1 recurring bug (COE07/08/09, ~33 patches over months) was a *truncated render after tab-switch*. Every prior fix targeted backend persistence / SSE / store-reconcile / boundary-dedup — and the bug always recurred because those layers were already innocent (store-level reconcile always returned full text). The actual defect was the React **render-source selector** (`TabView.tsx:152` dual-source `store ?? stale-prop` fallback) — a layer no prior fix had inspected. Fix = enforce ONE render source (MessageStore only; prop-fallback deleted), making divergence structurally impossible. Two meta-lessons: (1) when repeated fixes at one layer don't converge, STOP patching that layer and audit the untouched neighbor; (2) the entry was a LIVE DEV-gated repro probe, not another static patch — the bug was unreproducible at every statically-testable layer, so only live observation localized it (this was the long-standing P0 in Open Threads OT01).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **Unify scattered deciders by DELEGATION, not ABSORPTION, when the old unit is heavily tested** (RecoveryCoordinator, run_4988bfb4, 2026-06-25) — 8 independent kill-deciders unified into one RecoveryCoordinator. The blast-radius check decided the shape: HealingLoop had 1 prod caller but **5 test files** → the coordinator HOLDS HealingLoop (delegates breaker state) instead of replacing it, so all 5 test files stayed green untouched (DEC06). Owns only the DECISION (may-recover + what-kind + escalation); kill MECHANICS stay in SessionUnit. Multi-shape unification rule (PIT17): share what is TRULY universal (the enabled/user_stopped guard + the 7-verdict vocabulary), DISPATCH what differs (the gate — attempt-breaker vs cooldown vs bare-threshold vs graceful-escalation). The RecoveryTransaction lock then closed the `_crash_to_cold` TOCTOU (N concurrent callers → exactly 1 teardown) — recovery paths MUST have a forced-execution test (STEERING #11; the `self._pid` AttributeError class proved "compiles ≠ executes").
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **PermissionError is not ProcessLookupError** -- `os.kill(pid, 0)` raises `PermissionError` (subclass of `OSError`) for processes owned by other users. Catching `(OSError, ProcessLookupError)` treats alive-but-unowned processes as dead. Fix: catch `PermissionError` separately and treat as "alive". This matters for daemon conflict checks where the daemon runs as the same user but PID 1 (launchd) owns the port check socket. Pattern: any PID liveness check must handle 3 states: alive+ours, alive+theirs (PermissionError), dead (ProcessLookupError).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived -->

- [guideline] **Streaming-render cost lives in the renderer, not the transport — gate the expensive parse on `isStreaming`** (run_00e0e872, 2026-06-26) — "Streaming feels janky on long replies" was NOT a transport/SSE/store problem (those were all confirmed per-token-immediate + rAF-coalesced). The cost was `ContentBlockRenderer:50` feeding a growing `block.text` into MarkdownRenderer (4 remark/rehype plugins + KaTeX + highlight.js) on EVERY token → O(n²) re-parse over the stream. Fix = render plaintext (`whitespace-pre-wrap`) while `isStreaming`, switch to markdown on finish (the unchanged path every historical message already uses). Three reusable points: (1) when a "feels slow" complaint hits a streaming UI, profile the RENDER leaf before the data layer — per-token full re-parse is the classic O(n²) trap; (2) the safest perf fix on a bug-sensitive frontend is a presentation-leaf conditional that reads state and writes none — blast radius is provably zero (adversarial verified a-e); (3) the cross-tab stuck-state fear (OT01/COE07-09 history) was structurally absent BECAUSE `isStreaming` is per-tab + only the re-render-triggering `setIsStreaming` writes it + a 30s reconcile loop force-clears — proving the single-writer + reconcile-backstop architecture pays off when adding new state-dependent render branches.
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **After N transport-layer fixes don't hold, the bug is in the layer you never touched** (reconcile-gap, run_9db9f987, 2026-06-25) — The #1 recurring bug (COE07/08/09, ~33 patches over months) was a *truncated render after tab-switch*. Every prior fix targeted backend persistence / SSE / store-reconcile / boundary-dedup — and the bug always recurred because those layers were already innocent (store-level reconcile always returned full text). The actual defect was the React **render-source selector** (`TabView.tsx:152` dual-source `store ?? stale-prop` fallback) — a layer no prior fix had inspected. Fix = enforce ONE render source (MessageStore only; prop-fallback deleted), making divergence structurally impossible. Two meta-lessons: (1) when repeated fixes at one layer don't converge, STOP patching that layer and audit the untouched neighbor; (2) the entry was a LIVE DEV-gated repro probe, not another static patch — the bug was unreproducible at every statically-testable layer, so only live observation localized it (this was the long-standing P0 in Open Threads OT01).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **Unify scattered deciders by DELEGATION, not ABSORPTION, when the old unit is heavily tested** (RecoveryCoordinator, run_4988bfb4, 2026-06-25) — 8 independent kill-deciders unified into one RecoveryCoordinator. The blast-radius check decided the shape: HealingLoop had 1 prod caller but **5 test files** → the coordinator HOLDS HealingLoop (delegates breaker state) instead of replacing it, so all 5 test files stayed green untouched (DEC06). Owns only the DECISION (may-recover + what-kind + escalation); kill MECHANICS stay in SessionUnit. Multi-shape unification rule (PIT17): share what is TRULY universal (the enabled/user_stopped guard + the 7-verdict vocabulary), DISPATCH what differs (the gate — attempt-breaker vs cooldown vs bare-threshold vs graceful-escalation). The RecoveryTransaction lock then closed the `_crash_to_cold` TOCTOU (N concurrent callers → exactly 1 teardown) — recovery paths MUST have a forced-execution test (STEERING #11; the `self._pid` AttributeError class proved "compiles ≠ executes").
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **PermissionError is not ProcessLookupError** -- `os.kill(pid, 0)` raises `PermissionError` (subclass of `OSError`) for processes owned by other users. Catching `(OSError, ProcessLookupError)` treats alive-but-unowned processes as dead. Fix: catch `PermissionError` separately and treat as "alive". This matters for daemon conflict checks where the daemon runs as the same user but PID 1 (launchd) owns the port check socket. Pattern: any PID liveness check must handle 3 states: alive+ours, alive+theirs (PermissionError), dead (ProcessLookupError).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived -->

- [guideline] **Streaming-render cost lives in the renderer, not the transport — gate the expensive parse on `isStreaming`** (run_00e0e872, 2026-06-26) — "Streaming feels janky on long replies" was NOT a transport/SSE/store problem (those were all confirmed per-token-immediate + rAF-coalesced). The cost was `ContentBlockRenderer:50` feeding a growing `block.text` into MarkdownRenderer (4 remark/rehype plugins + KaTeX + highlight.js) on EVERY token → O(n²) re-parse over the stream. Fix = render plaintext (`whitespace-pre-wrap`) while `isStreaming`, switch to markdown on finish (the unchanged path every historical message already uses). Three reusable points: (1) when a "feels slow" complaint hits a streaming UI, profile the RENDER leaf before the data layer — per-token full re-parse is the classic O(n²) trap; (2) the safest perf fix on a bug-sensitive frontend is a presentation-leaf conditional that reads state and writes none — blast radius is provably zero (adversarial verified a-e); (3) the cross-tab stuck-state fear (OT01/COE07-09 history) was structurally absent BECAUSE `isStreaming` is per-tab + only the re-render-triggering `setIsStreaming` writes it + a 30s reconcile loop force-clears — proving the single-writer + reconcile-backstop architecture pays off when adding new state-dependent render branches.
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **After N transport-layer fixes don't hold, the bug is in the layer you never touched** (reconcile-gap, run_9db9f987, 2026-06-25) — The #1 recurring bug (COE07/08/09, ~33 patches over months) was a *truncated render after tab-switch*. Every prior fix targeted backend persistence / SSE / store-reconcile / boundary-dedup — and the bug always recurred because those layers were already innocent (store-level reconcile always returned full text). The actual defect was the React **render-source selector** (`TabView.tsx:152` dual-source `store ?? stale-prop` fallback) — a layer no prior fix had inspected. Fix = enforce ONE render source (MessageStore only; prop-fallback deleted), making divergence structurally impossible. Two meta-lessons: (1) when repeated fixes at one layer don't converge, STOP patching that layer and audit the untouched neighbor; (2) the entry was a LIVE DEV-gated repro probe, not another static patch — the bug was unreproducible at every statically-testable layer, so only live observation localized it (this was the long-standing P0 in Open Threads OT01).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **Unify scattered deciders by DELEGATION, not ABSORPTION, when the old unit is heavily tested** (RecoveryCoordinator, run_4988bfb4, 2026-06-25) — 8 independent kill-deciders unified into one RecoveryCoordinator. The blast-radius check decided the shape: HealingLoop had 1 prod caller but **5 test files** → the coordinator HOLDS HealingLoop (delegates breaker state) instead of replacing it, so all 5 test files stayed green untouched (DEC06). Owns only the DECISION (may-recover + what-kind + escalation); kill MECHANICS stay in SessionUnit. Multi-shape unification rule (PIT17): share what is TRULY universal (the enabled/user_stopped guard + the 7-verdict vocabulary), DISPATCH what differs (the gate — attempt-breaker vs cooldown vs bare-threshold vs graceful-escalation). The RecoveryTransaction lock then closed the `_crash_to_cold` TOCTOU (N concurrent callers → exactly 1 teardown) — recovery paths MUST have a forced-execution test (STEERING #11; the `self._pid` AttributeError class proved "compiles ≠ executes").
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **PermissionError is not ProcessLookupError** -- `os.kill(pid, 0)` raises `PermissionError` (subclass of `OSError`) for processes owned by other users. Catching `(OSError, ProcessLookupError)` treats alive-but-unowned processes as dead. Fix: catch `PermissionError` separately and treat as "alive". This matters for daemon conflict checks where the daemon runs as the same user but PID 1 (launchd) owns the port check socket. Pattern: any PID liveness check must handle 3 states: alive+ours, alive+theirs (PermissionError), dead (ProcessLookupError).

- [guideline] **Streaming-render cost lives in the renderer, not the transport — gate the expensive parse on `isStreaming`** (run_00e0e872, 2026-06-26) — "Streaming feels janky on long replies" was NOT a transport/SSE/store problem (those were all confirmed per-token-immediate + rAF-coalesced). The cost was `ContentBlockRenderer:50` feeding a growing `block.text` into MarkdownRenderer (4 remark/rehype plugins + KaTeX + highlight.js) on EVERY token → O(n²) re-parse over the stream. Fix = render plaintext (`whitespace-pre-wrap`) while `isStreaming`, switch to markdown on finish (the unchanged path every historical message already uses). Three reusable points: (1) when a "feels slow" complaint hits a streaming UI, profile the RENDER leaf before the data layer — per-token full re-parse is the classic O(n²) trap; (2) the safest perf fix on a bug-sensitive frontend is a presentation-leaf conditional that reads state and writes none — blast radius is provably zero (adversarial verified a-e); (3) the cross-tab stuck-state fear (OT01/COE07-09 history) was structurally absent BECAUSE `isStreaming` is per-tab + only the re-render-triggering `setIsStreaming` writes it + a 30s reconcile loop force-clears — proving the single-writer + reconcile-backstop architecture pays off when adding new state-dependent render branches.
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **After N transport-layer fixes don't hold, the bug is in the layer you never touched** (reconcile-gap, run_9db9f987, 2026-06-25) — The #1 recurring bug (COE07/08/09, ~33 patches over months) was a *truncated render after tab-switch*. Every prior fix targeted backend persistence / SSE / store-reconcile / boundary-dedup — and the bug always recurred because those layers were already innocent (store-level reconcile always returned full text). The actual defect was the React **render-source selector** (`TabView.tsx:152` dual-source `store ?? stale-prop` fallback) — a layer no prior fix had inspected. Fix = enforce ONE render source (MessageStore only; prop-fallback deleted), making divergence structurally impossible. Two meta-lessons: (1) when repeated fixes at one layer don't converge, STOP patching that layer and audit the untouched neighbor; (2) the entry was a LIVE DEV-gated repro probe, not another static patch — the bug was unreproducible at every statically-testable layer, so only live observation localized it (this was the long-standing P0 in Open Threads OT01).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **Unify scattered deciders by DELEGATION, not ABSORPTION, when the old unit is heavily tested** (RecoveryCoordinator, run_4988bfb4, 2026-06-25) — 8 independent kill-deciders unified into one RecoveryCoordinator. The blast-radius check decided the shape: HealingLoop had 1 prod caller but **5 test files** → the coordinator HOLDS HealingLoop (delegates breaker state) instead of replacing it, so all 5 test files stayed green untouched (DEC06). Owns only the DECISION (may-recover + what-kind + escalation); kill MECHANICS stay in SessionUnit. Multi-shape unification rule (PIT17): share what is TRULY universal (the enabled/user_stopped guard + the 7-verdict vocabulary), DISPATCH what differs (the gate — attempt-breaker vs cooldown vs bare-threshold vs graceful-escalation). The RecoveryTransaction lock then closed the `_crash_to_cold` TOCTOU (N concurrent callers → exactly 1 teardown) — recovery paths MUST have a forced-execution test (STEERING #11; the `self._pid` AttributeError class proved "compiles ≠ executes").

- [guideline] **PermissionError is not ProcessLookupError** -- `os.kill(pid, 0)` raises `PermissionError` (subclass of `OSError`) for processes owned by other users. Catching `(OSError, ProcessLookupError)` treats alive-but-unowned processes as dead. Fix: catch `PermissionError` separately and treat as "alive". This matters for daemon conflict checks where the daemon runs as the same user but PID 1 (launchd) owns the port check socket. Pattern: any PID liveness check must handle 3 states: alive+ours, alive+theirs (PermissionError), dead (ProcessLookupError).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived -->

- [guideline] **Streaming-render cost lives in the renderer, not the transport — gate the expensive parse on `isStreaming`** (run_00e0e872, 2026-06-26) — "Streaming feels janky on long replies" was NOT a transport/SSE/store problem (those were all confirmed per-token-immediate + rAF-coalesced). The cost was `ContentBlockRenderer:50` feeding a growing `block.text` into MarkdownRenderer (4 remark/rehype plugins + KaTeX + highlight.js) on EVERY token → O(n²) re-parse over the stream. Fix = render plaintext (`whitespace-pre-wrap`) while `isStreaming`, switch to markdown on finish (the unchanged path every historical message already uses). Three reusable points: (1) when a "feels slow" complaint hits a streaming UI, profile the RENDER leaf before the data layer — per-token full re-parse is the classic O(n²) trap; (2) the safest perf fix on a bug-sensitive frontend is a presentation-leaf conditional that reads state and writes none — blast radius is provably zero (adversarial verified a-e); (3) the cross-tab stuck-state fear (OT01/COE07-09 history) was structurally absent BECAUSE `isStreaming` is per-tab + only the re-render-triggering `setIsStreaming` writes it + a 30s reconcile loop force-clears — proving the single-writer + reconcile-backstop architecture pays off when adding new state-dependent render branches.
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **After N transport-layer fixes don't hold, the bug is in the layer you never touched** (reconcile-gap, run_9db9f987, 2026-06-25) — The #1 recurring bug (COE07/08/09, ~33 patches over months) was a *truncated render after tab-switch*. Every prior fix targeted backend persistence / SSE / store-reconcile / boundary-dedup — and the bug always recurred because those layers were already innocent (store-level reconcile always returned full text). The actual defect was the React **render-source selector** (`TabView.tsx:152` dual-source `store ?? stale-prop` fallback) — a layer no prior fix had inspected. Fix = enforce ONE render source (MessageStore only; prop-fallback deleted), making divergence structurally impossible. Two meta-lessons: (1) when repeated fixes at one layer don't converge, STOP patching that layer and audit the untouched neighbor; (2) the entry was a LIVE DEV-gated repro probe, not another static patch — the bug was unreproducible at every statically-testable layer, so only live observation localized it (this was the long-standing P0 in Open Threads OT01).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **Unify scattered deciders by DELEGATION, not ABSORPTION, when the old unit is heavily tested** (RecoveryCoordinator, run_4988bfb4, 2026-06-25) — 8 independent kill-deciders unified into one RecoveryCoordinator. The blast-radius check decided the shape: HealingLoop had 1 prod caller but **5 test files** → the coordinator HOLDS HealingLoop (delegates breaker state) instead of replacing it, so all 5 test files stayed green untouched (DEC06). Owns only the DECISION (may-recover + what-kind + escalation); kill MECHANICS stay in SessionUnit. Multi-shape unification rule (PIT17): share what is TRULY universal (the enabled/user_stopped guard + the 7-verdict vocabulary), DISPATCH what differs (the gate — attempt-breaker vs cooldown vs bare-threshold vs graceful-escalation). The RecoveryTransaction lock then closed the `_crash_to_cold` TOCTOU (N concurrent callers → exactly 1 teardown) — recovery paths MUST have a forced-execution test (STEERING #11; the `self._pid` AttributeError class proved "compiles ≠ executes").
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **PermissionError is not ProcessLookupError** -- `os.kill(pid, 0)` raises `PermissionError` (subclass of `OSError`) for processes owned by other users. Catching `(OSError, ProcessLookupError)` treats alive-but-unowned processes as dead. Fix: catch `PermissionError` separately and treat as "alive". This matters for daemon conflict checks where the daemon runs as the same user but PID 1 (launchd) owns the port check socket. Pattern: any PID liveness check must handle 3 states: alive+ours, alive+theirs (PermissionError), dead (ProcessLookupError).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived -->

- [guideline] **Streaming-render cost lives in the renderer, not the transport — gate the expensive parse on `isStreaming`** (run_00e0e872, 2026-06-26) — "Streaming feels janky on long replies" was NOT a transport/SSE/store problem (those were all confirmed per-token-immediate + rAF-coalesced). The cost was `ContentBlockRenderer:50` feeding a growing `block.text` into MarkdownRenderer (4 remark/rehype plugins + KaTeX + highlight.js) on EVERY token → O(n²) re-parse over the stream. Fix = render plaintext (`whitespace-pre-wrap`) while `isStreaming`, switch to markdown on finish (the unchanged path every historical message already uses). Three reusable points: (1) when a "feels slow" complaint hits a streaming UI, profile the RENDER leaf before the data layer — per-token full re-parse is the classic O(n²) trap; (2) the safest perf fix on a bug-sensitive frontend is a presentation-leaf conditional that reads state and writes none — blast radius is provably zero (adversarial verified a-e); (3) the cross-tab stuck-state fear (OT01/COE07-09 history) was structurally absent BECAUSE `isStreaming` is per-tab + only the re-render-triggering `setIsStreaming` writes it + a 30s reconcile loop force-clears — proving the single-writer + reconcile-backstop architecture pays off when adding new state-dependent render branches.
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **After N transport-layer fixes don't hold, the bug is in the layer you never touched** (reconcile-gap, run_9db9f987, 2026-06-25) — The #1 recurring bug (COE07/08/09, ~33 patches over months) was a *truncated render after tab-switch*. Every prior fix targeted backend persistence / SSE / store-reconcile / boundary-dedup — and the bug always recurred because those layers were already innocent (store-level reconcile always returned full text). The actual defect was the React **render-source selector** (`TabView.tsx:152` dual-source `store ?? stale-prop` fallback) — a layer no prior fix had inspected. Fix = enforce ONE render source (MessageStore only; prop-fallback deleted), making divergence structurally impossible. Two meta-lessons: (1) when repeated fixes at one layer don't converge, STOP patching that layer and audit the untouched neighbor; (2) the entry was a LIVE DEV-gated repro probe, not another static patch — the bug was unreproducible at every statically-testable layer, so only live observation localized it (this was the long-standing P0 in Open Threads OT01).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **Unify scattered deciders by DELEGATION, not ABSORPTION, when the old unit is heavily tested** (RecoveryCoordinator, run_4988bfb4, 2026-06-25) — 8 independent kill-deciders unified into one RecoveryCoordinator. The blast-radius check decided the shape: HealingLoop had 1 prod caller but **5 test files** → the coordinator HOLDS HealingLoop (delegates breaker state) instead of replacing it, so all 5 test files stayed green untouched (DEC06). Owns only the DECISION (may-recover + what-kind + escalation); kill MECHANICS stay in SessionUnit. Multi-shape unification rule (PIT17): share what is TRULY universal (the enabled/user_stopped guard + the 7-verdict vocabulary), DISPATCH what differs (the gate — attempt-breaker vs cooldown vs bare-threshold vs graceful-escalation). The RecoveryTransaction lock then closed the `_crash_to_cold` TOCTOU (N concurrent callers → exactly 1 teardown) — recovery paths MUST have a forced-execution test (STEERING #11; the `self._pid` AttributeError class proved "compiles ≠ executes").
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **Streaming-render cost lives in the renderer, not the transport — gate the expensive parse on `isStreaming`** (run_00e0e872, 2026-06-26) — "Streaming feels janky on long replies" was NOT a transport/SSE/store problem (those were all confirmed per-token-immediate + rAF-coalesced). The cost was `ContentBlockRenderer:50` feeding a growing `block.text` into MarkdownRenderer (4 remark/rehype plugins + KaTeX + highlight.js) on EVERY token → O(n²) re-parse over the stream. Fix = render plaintext (`whitespace-pre-wrap`) while `isStreaming`, switch to markdown on finish (the unchanged path every historical message already uses). Three reusable points: (1) when a "feels slow" complaint hits a streaming UI, profile the RENDER leaf before the data layer — per-token full re-parse is the classic O(n²) trap; (2) the safest perf fix on a bug-sensitive frontend is a presentation-leaf conditional that reads state and writes none — blast radius is provably zero (adversarial verified a-e); (3) the cross-tab stuck-state fear (OT01/COE07-09 history) was structurally absent BECAUSE `isStreaming` is per-tab + only the re-render-triggering `setIsStreaming` writes it + a 30s reconcile loop force-clears — proving the single-writer + reconcile-backstop architecture pays off when adding new state-dependent render branches.
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **After N transport-layer fixes don't hold, the bug is in the layer you never touched** (reconcile-gap, run_9db9f987, 2026-06-25) — The #1 recurring bug (COE07/08/09, ~33 patches over months) was a *truncated render after tab-switch*. Every prior fix targeted backend persistence / SSE / store-reconcile / boundary-dedup — and the bug always recurred because those layers were already innocent (store-level reconcile always returned full text). The actual defect was the React **render-source selector** (`TabView.tsx:152` dual-source `store ?? stale-prop` fallback) — a layer no prior fix had inspected. Fix = enforce ONE render source (MessageStore only; prop-fallback deleted), making divergence structurally impossible. Two meta-lessons: (1) when repeated fixes at one layer don't converge, STOP patching that layer and audit the untouched neighbor; (2) the entry was a LIVE DEV-gated repro probe, not another static patch — the bug was unreproducible at every statically-testable layer, so only live observation localized it (this was the long-standing P0 in Open Threads OT01).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **Unify scattered deciders by DELEGATION, not ABSORPTION, when the old unit is heavily tested** (RecoveryCoordinator, run_4988bfb4, 2026-06-25) — 8 independent kill-deciders unified into one RecoveryCoordinator. The blast-radius check decided the shape: HealingLoop had 1 prod caller but **5 test files** → the coordinator HOLDS HealingLoop (delegates breaker state) instead of replacing it, so all 5 test files stayed green untouched (DEC06). Owns only the DECISION (may-recover + what-kind + escalation); kill MECHANICS stay in SessionUnit. Multi-shape unification rule (PIT17): share what is TRULY universal (the enabled/user_stopped guard + the 7-verdict vocabulary), DISPATCH what differs (the gate — attempt-breaker vs cooldown vs bare-threshold vs graceful-escalation). The RecoveryTransaction lock then closed the `_crash_to_cold` TOCTOU (N concurrent callers → exactly 1 teardown) — recovery paths MUST have a forced-execution test (STEERING #11; the `self._pid` AttributeError class proved "compiles ≠ executes").
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **PermissionError is not ProcessLookupError** -- `os.kill(pid, 0)` raises `PermissionError` (subclass of `OSError`) for processes owned by other users. Catching `(OSError, ProcessLookupError)` treats alive-but-unowned processes as dead. Fix: catch `PermissionError` separately and treat as "alive". This matters for daemon conflict checks where the daemon runs as the same user but PID 1 (launchd) owns the port check socket. Pattern: any PID liveness check must handle 3 states: alive+ours, alive+theirs (PermissionError), dead (ProcessLookupError).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived -->

- [guideline] **Streaming-render cost lives in the renderer, not the transport — gate the expensive parse on `isStreaming`** (run_00e0e872, 2026-06-26) — "Streaming feels janky on long replies" was NOT a transport/SSE/store problem (those were all confirmed per-token-immediate + rAF-coalesced). The cost was `ContentBlockRenderer:50` feeding a growing `block.text` into MarkdownRenderer (4 remark/rehype plugins + KaTeX + highlight.js) on EVERY token → O(n²) re-parse over the stream. Fix = render plaintext (`whitespace-pre-wrap`) while `isStreaming`, switch to markdown on finish (the unchanged path every historical message already uses). Three reusable points: (1) when a "feels slow" complaint hits a streaming UI, profile the RENDER leaf before the data layer — per-token full re-parse is the classic O(n²) trap; (2) the safest perf fix on a bug-sensitive frontend is a presentation-leaf conditional that reads state and writes none — blast radius is provably zero (adversarial verified a-e); (3) the cross-tab stuck-state fear (OT01/COE07-09 history) was structurally absent BECAUSE `isStreaming` is per-tab + only the re-render-triggering `setIsStreaming` writes it + a 30s reconcile loop force-clears — proving the single-writer + reconcile-backstop architecture pays off when adding new state-dependent render branches.
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **After N transport-layer fixes don't hold, the bug is in the layer you never touched** (reconcile-gap, run_9db9f987, 2026-06-25) — The #1 recurring bug (COE07/08/09, ~33 patches over months) was a *truncated render after tab-switch*. Every prior fix targeted backend persistence / SSE / store-reconcile / boundary-dedup — and the bug always recurred because those layers were already innocent (store-level reconcile always returned full text). The actual defect was the React **render-source selector** (`TabView.tsx:152` dual-source `store ?? stale-prop` fallback) — a layer no prior fix had inspected. Fix = enforce ONE render source (MessageStore only; prop-fallback deleted), making divergence structurally impossible. Two meta-lessons: (1) when repeated fixes at one layer don't converge, STOP patching that layer and audit the untouched neighbor; (2) the entry was a LIVE DEV-gated repro probe, not another static patch — the bug was unreproducible at every statically-testable layer, so only live observation localized it (this was the long-standing P0 in Open Threads OT01).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **Unify scattered deciders by DELEGATION, not ABSORPTION, when the old unit is heavily tested** (RecoveryCoordinator, run_4988bfb4, 2026-06-25) — 8 independent kill-deciders unified into one RecoveryCoordinator. The blast-radius check decided the shape: HealingLoop had 1 prod caller but **5 test files** → the coordinator HOLDS HealingLoop (delegates breaker state) instead of replacing it, so all 5 test files stayed green untouched (DEC06). Owns only the DECISION (may-recover + what-kind + escalation); kill MECHANICS stay in SessionUnit. Multi-shape unification rule (PIT17): share what is TRULY universal (the enabled/user_stopped guard + the 7-verdict vocabulary), DISPATCH what differs (the gate — attempt-breaker vs cooldown vs bare-threshold vs graceful-escalation). The RecoveryTransaction lock then closed the `_crash_to_cold` TOCTOU (N concurrent callers → exactly 1 teardown) — recovery paths MUST have a forced-execution test (STEERING #11; the `self._pid` AttributeError class proved "compiles ≠ executes").
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **PermissionError is not ProcessLookupError** -- `os.kill(pid, 0)` raises `PermissionError` (subclass of `OSError`) for processes owned by other users. Catching `(OSError, ProcessLookupError)` treats alive-but-unowned processes as dead. Fix: catch `PermissionError` separately and treat as "alive". This matters for daemon conflict checks where the daemon runs as the same user but PID 1 (launchd) owns the port check socket. Pattern: any PID liveness check must handle 3 states: alive+ours, alive+theirs (PermissionError), dead (ProcessLookupError).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived -->

- [guideline] **Streaming-render cost lives in the renderer, not the transport — gate the expensive parse on `isStreaming`** (run_00e0e872, 2026-06-26) — "Streaming feels janky on long replies" was NOT a transport/SSE/store problem (those were all confirmed per-token-immediate + rAF-coalesced). The cost was `ContentBlockRenderer:50` feeding a growing `block.text` into MarkdownRenderer (4 remark/rehype plugins + KaTeX + highlight.js) on EVERY token → O(n²) re-parse over the stream. Fix = render plaintext (`whitespace-pre-wrap`) while `isStreaming`, switch to markdown on finish (the unchanged path every historical message already uses). Three reusable points: (1) when a "feels slow" complaint hits a streaming UI, profile the RENDER leaf before the data layer — per-token full re-parse is the classic O(n²) trap; (2) the safest perf fix on a bug-sensitive frontend is a presentation-leaf conditional that reads state and writes none — blast radius is provably zero (adversarial verified a-e); (3) the cross-tab stuck-state fear (OT01/COE07-09 history) was structurally absent BECAUSE `isStreaming` is per-tab + only the re-render-triggering `setIsStreaming` writes it + a 30s reconcile loop force-clears — proving the single-writer + reconcile-backstop architecture pays off when adding new state-dependent render branches.
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **After N transport-layer fixes don't hold, the bug is in the layer you never touched** (reconcile-gap, run_9db9f987, 2026-06-25) — The #1 recurring bug (COE07/08/09, ~33 patches over months) was a *truncated render after tab-switch*. Every prior fix targeted backend persistence / SSE / store-reconcile / boundary-dedup — and the bug always recurred because those layers were already innocent (store-level reconcile always returned full text). The actual defect was the React **render-source selector** (`TabView.tsx:152` dual-source `store ?? stale-prop` fallback) — a layer no prior fix had inspected. Fix = enforce ONE render source (MessageStore only; prop-fallback deleted), making divergence structurally impossible. Two meta-lessons: (1) when repeated fixes at one layer don't converge, STOP patching that layer and audit the untouched neighbor; (2) the entry was a LIVE DEV-gated repro probe, not another static patch — the bug was unreproducible at every statically-testable layer, so only live observation localized it (this was the long-standing P0 in Open Threads OT01).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **Unify scattered deciders by DELEGATION, not ABSORPTION, when the old unit is heavily tested** (RecoveryCoordinator, run_4988bfb4, 2026-06-25) — 8 independent kill-deciders unified into one RecoveryCoordinator. The blast-radius check decided the shape: HealingLoop had 1 prod caller but **5 test files** → the coordinator HOLDS HealingLoop (delegates breaker state) instead of replacing it, so all 5 test files stayed green untouched (DEC06). Owns only the DECISION (may-recover + what-kind + escalation); kill MECHANICS stay in SessionUnit. Multi-shape unification rule (PIT17): share what is TRULY universal (the enabled/user_stopped guard + the 7-verdict vocabulary), DISPATCH what differs (the gate — attempt-breaker vs cooldown vs bare-threshold vs graceful-escalation). The RecoveryTransaction lock then closed the `_crash_to_cold` TOCTOU (N concurrent callers → exactly 1 teardown) — recovery paths MUST have a forced-execution test (STEERING #11; the `self._pid` AttributeError class proved "compiles ≠ executes").
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **PermissionError is not ProcessLookupError** -- `os.kill(pid, 0)` raises `PermissionError` (subclass of `OSError`) for processes owned by other users. Catching `(OSError, ProcessLookupError)` treats alive-but-unowned processes as dead. Fix: catch `PermissionError` separately and treat as "alive". This matters for daemon conflict checks where the daemon runs as the same user but PID 1 (launchd) owns the port check socket. Pattern: any PID liveness check must handle 3 states: alive+ours, alive+theirs (PermissionError), dead (ProcessLookupError).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived -->

- [guideline] **Streaming-render cost lives in the renderer, not the transport — gate the expensive parse on `isStreaming`** (run_00e0e872, 2026-06-26) — "Streaming feels janky on long replies" was NOT a transport/SSE/store problem (those were all confirmed per-token-immediate + rAF-coalesced). The cost was `ContentBlockRenderer:50` feeding a growing `block.text` into MarkdownRenderer (4 remark/rehype plugins + KaTeX + highlight.js) on EVERY token → O(n²) re-parse over the stream. Fix = render plaintext (`whitespace-pre-wrap`) while `isStreaming`, switch to markdown on finish (the unchanged path every historical message already uses). Three reusable points: (1) when a "feels slow" complaint hits a streaming UI, profile the RENDER leaf before the data layer — per-token full re-parse is the classic O(n²) trap; (2) the safest perf fix on a bug-sensitive frontend is a presentation-leaf conditional that reads state and writes none — blast radius is provably zero (adversarial verified a-e); (3) the cross-tab stuck-state fear (OT01/COE07-09 history) was structurally absent BECAUSE `isStreaming` is per-tab + only the re-render-triggering `setIsStreaming` writes it + a 30s reconcile loop force-clears — proving the single-writer + reconcile-backstop architecture pays off when adding new state-dependent render branches.
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **After N transport-layer fixes don't hold, the bug is in the layer you never touched** (reconcile-gap, run_9db9f987, 2026-06-25) — The #1 recurring bug (COE07/08/09, ~33 patches over months) was a *truncated render after tab-switch*. Every prior fix targeted backend persistence / SSE / store-reconcile / boundary-dedup — and the bug always recurred because those layers were already innocent (store-level reconcile always returned full text). The actual defect was the React **render-source selector** (`TabView.tsx:152` dual-source `store ?? stale-prop` fallback) — a layer no prior fix had inspected. Fix = enforce ONE render source (MessageStore only; prop-fallback deleted), making divergence structurally impossible. Two meta-lessons: (1) when repeated fixes at one layer don't converge, STOP patching that layer and audit the untouched neighbor; (2) the entry was a LIVE DEV-gated repro probe, not another static patch — the bug was unreproducible at every statically-testable layer, so only live observation localized it (this was the long-standing P0 in Open Threads OT01).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **Unify scattered deciders by DELEGATION, not ABSORPTION, when the old unit is heavily tested** (RecoveryCoordinator, run_4988bfb4, 2026-06-25) — 8 independent kill-deciders unified into one RecoveryCoordinator. The blast-radius check decided the shape: HealingLoop had 1 prod caller but **5 test files** → the coordinator HOLDS HealingLoop (delegates breaker state) instead of replacing it, so all 5 test files stayed green untouched (DEC06). Owns only the DECISION (may-recover + what-kind + escalation); kill MECHANICS stay in SessionUnit. Multi-shape unification rule (PIT17): share what is TRULY universal (the enabled/user_stopped guard + the 7-verdict vocabulary), DISPATCH what differs (the gate — attempt-breaker vs cooldown vs bare-threshold vs graceful-escalation). The RecoveryTransaction lock then closed the `_crash_to_cold` TOCTOU (N concurrent callers → exactly 1 teardown) — recovery paths MUST have a forced-execution test (STEERING #11; the `self._pid` AttributeError class proved "compiles ≠ executes").
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **PermissionError is not ProcessLookupError** -- `os.kill(pid, 0)` raises `PermissionError` (subclass of `OSError`) for processes owned by other users. Catching `(OSError, ProcessLookupError)` treats alive-but-unowned processes as dead. Fix: catch `PermissionError` separately and treat as "alive". This matters for daemon conflict checks where the daemon runs as the same user but PID 1 (launchd) owns the port check socket. Pattern: any PID liveness check must handle 3 states: alive+ours, alive+theirs (PermissionError), dead (ProcessLookupError).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived -->

- [guideline] **Streaming-render cost lives in the renderer, not the transport — gate the expensive parse on `isStreaming`** (run_00e0e872, 2026-06-26) — "Streaming feels janky on long replies" was NOT a transport/SSE/store problem (those were all confirmed per-token-immediate + rAF-coalesced). The cost was `ContentBlockRenderer:50` feeding a growing `block.text` into MarkdownRenderer (4 remark/rehype plugins + KaTeX + highlight.js) on EVERY token → O(n²) re-parse over the stream. Fix = render plaintext (`whitespace-pre-wrap`) while `isStreaming`, switch to markdown on finish (the unchanged path every historical message already uses). Three reusable points: (1) when a "feels slow" complaint hits a streaming UI, profile the RENDER leaf before the data layer — per-token full re-parse is the classic O(n²) trap; (2) the safest perf fix on a bug-sensitive frontend is a presentation-leaf conditional that reads state and writes none — blast radius is provably zero (adversarial verified a-e); (3) the cross-tab stuck-state fear (OT01/COE07-09 history) was structurally absent BECAUSE `isStreaming` is per-tab + only the re-render-triggering `setIsStreaming` writes it + a 30s reconcile loop force-clears — proving the single-writer + reconcile-backstop architecture pays off when adding new state-dependent render branches.
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **After N transport-layer fixes don't hold, the bug is in the layer you never touched** (reconcile-gap, run_9db9f987, 2026-06-25) — The #1 recurring bug (COE07/08/09, ~33 patches over months) was a *truncated render after tab-switch*. Every prior fix targeted backend persistence / SSE / store-reconcile / boundary-dedup — and the bug always recurred because those layers were already innocent (store-level reconcile always returned full text). The actual defect was the React **render-source selector** (`TabView.tsx:152` dual-source `store ?? stale-prop` fallback) — a layer no prior fix had inspected. Fix = enforce ONE render source (MessageStore only; prop-fallback deleted), making divergence structurally impossible. Two meta-lessons: (1) when repeated fixes at one layer don't converge, STOP patching that layer and audit the untouched neighbor; (2) the entry was a LIVE DEV-gated repro probe, not another static patch — the bug was unreproducible at every statically-testable layer, so only live observation localized it (this was the long-standing P0 in Open Threads OT01).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **Unify scattered deciders by DELEGATION, not ABSORPTION, when the old unit is heavily tested** (RecoveryCoordinator, run_4988bfb4, 2026-06-25) — 8 independent kill-deciders unified into one RecoveryCoordinator. The blast-radius check decided the shape: HealingLoop had 1 prod caller but **5 test files** → the coordinator HOLDS HealingLoop (delegates breaker state) instead of replacing it, so all 5 test files stayed green untouched (DEC06). Owns only the DECISION (may-recover + what-kind + escalation); kill MECHANICS stay in SessionUnit. Multi-shape unification rule (PIT17): share what is TRULY universal (the enabled/user_stopped guard + the 7-verdict vocabulary), DISPATCH what differs (the gate — attempt-breaker vs cooldown vs bare-threshold vs graceful-escalation). The RecoveryTransaction lock then closed the `_crash_to_cold` TOCTOU (N concurrent callers → exactly 1 teardown) — recovery paths MUST have a forced-execution test (STEERING #11; the `self._pid` AttributeError class proved "compiles ≠ executes").
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **PermissionError is not ProcessLookupError** -- `os.kill(pid, 0)` raises `PermissionError` (subclass of `OSError`) for processes owned by other users. Catching `(OSError, ProcessLookupError)` treats alive-but-unowned processes as dead. Fix: catch `PermissionError` separately and treat as "alive". This matters for daemon conflict checks where the daemon runs as the same user but PID 1 (launchd) owns the port check socket. Pattern: any PID liveness check must handle 3 states: alive+ours, alive+theirs (PermissionError), dead (ProcessLookupError).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived -->

The cost was `ContentBlockRenderer:50` feeding a growing `block.text` into MarkdownRenderer (4 remark/rehype plugins + KaTeX + highlight.js) on EVERY token → O(n²) re-parse over the stream. Fix = render plaintext (`whitespace-pre-wrap`) while `isStreaming`, switch to markdown on finish (the unchanged path every historical message already uses). Three reusable points: (1) when a "feels slow" complaint hits a streaming UI, profile the RENDER leaf before the data layer — per-token full re-parse is the classic O(n²) trap; (2) the safest perf fix on a bug-sensitive frontend is a presentation-leaf conditional that reads state and writes none — blast radius is provably zero (adversarial verified a-e); (3) the cross-tab stuck-state fear (OT01/COE07-09 history) was structurally absent BECAUSE `isStreaming` is per-tab + only the re-render-triggering `setIsStreaming` writes it + a 30s reconcile loop force-clears — proving the single-writer + reconcile-backstop architecture pays off when adding new state-dependent render branches.
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **After N transport-layer fixes don't hold, the bug is in the layer you never touched** (reconcile-gap, run_9db9f987, 2026-06-25) — The #1 recurring bug (COE07/08/09, ~33 patches over months) was a *truncated render after tab-switch*. Every prior fix targeted backend persistence / SSE / store-reconcile / boundary-dedup — and the bug always recurred because those layers were already innocent (store-level reconcile always returned full text). The actual defect was the React **render-source selector** (`TabView.tsx:152` dual-source `store ?? stale-prop` fallback) — a layer no prior fix had inspected. Fix = enforce ONE render source (MessageStore only; prop-fallback deleted), making divergence structurally impossible. Two meta-lessons: (1) when repeated fixes at one layer don't converge, STOP patching that layer and audit the untouched neighbor; (2) the entry was a LIVE DEV-gated repro probe, not another static patch — the bug was unreproducible at every statically-testable layer, so only live observation localized it (this was the long-standing P0 in Open Threads OT01).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived | source:manual -->

- [guideline] **Unify scattered deciders by DELEGATION, not ABSORPTION, when the old unit is heavily tested** (RecoveryCoordinator, run_4988bfb4, 2026-06-25) — 8 independent kill-deciders unified into one RecoveryCoordinator. The blast-radius check decided the shape: HealingLoop had 1 prod caller but **5 test files** → the coordinator HOLDS HealingLoop (delegates breaker state) instead of replacing it, so all 5 test files stayed green untouched (DEC06). Owns only the DECISION (may-recover + what-kind + escalation); kill MECHANICS stay in SessionUnit. Multi-shape unification rule (PIT17): share what is TRULY universal (the enabled/user_stopped guard + the 7-verdict vocabulary), DISPATCH what differs (the gate — attempt-breaker vs cooldown vs bare-threshold vs graceful-escalation). The RecoveryTransaction lock then closed the `_crash_to_cold` TOCTOU (N concurrent callers → exactly 1 teardown) — recovery paths MUST have a forced-execution test (STEERING #11; the `self._pid` AttributeError class proved "compiles ≠ executes").

- [guideline] **PermissionError is not ProcessLookupError** -- `os.kill(pid, 0)` raises `PermissionError` (subclass of `OSError`) for processes owned by other users. Catching `(OSError, ProcessLookupError)` treats alive-but-unowned processes as dead. Fix: catch `PermissionError` separately and treat as "alive". This matters for daemon conflict checks where the daemon runs as the same user but PID 1 (launchd) owns the port check socket. Pattern: any PID liveness check must handle 3 states: alive+ours, alive+theirs (PermissionError), dead (ProcessLookupError).
  <!-- ref:0 | last:none | decay:archived -->

Two meta-lessons: (1) when repeated fixes at one layer don't converge, STOP patching that layer and audit the untouched neighbor; (2) the entry was a LIVE DEV-gated repro probe, not another static patch — the bug was unreproducible at every statically-testable layer, so only live observation localized it (this was the long-standing P0 in Open Threads OT01).
